value: COMEX gold futures lead London OTC spot: ILS about 66% after 2007 (above 80% 2002-2007); IS and CS above 90% after 2006
detail: Hauptfleisch, Putnins and Lucey, Journal of Futures Markets 36(6) 2016 (accepted manuscript, UTS repository). New York futures (GC) contribute more to gold price discovery than London spot. After Globex, US futures lead irrespective of market hours. Bears on whether GC is the leader of the gold underlying (it leads), not on MGC's share (MGC not studied).
quote: ILS tells a slightly different story. The futures market in the first year of our sample has an ILS of 66%, which rises above 80% for the years 2002 to 2007, after which it falls slightly and remains stable around 66%. ... After the move to the GLOBEX platform and introduction of international participation incentives in the futures market, intraday price discovery variation declines with US futures taking a consistent lead irrespective of market hours.

quote: The results indicate that it is Comex, followed by the SHFE, not the LME which plays the most important role in copper price discovery.

value: US macro releases 08:30 ET (nonfarm payrolls, durable goods largest), 09:15 ET and 10:00 ET sets; monthly or less frequent
window: 2002-01 to 2008-12, 5-minute returns, GC SI HG futures
detail: Elder, Miao and Ramchander, Journal of Banking & Finance 2012 (repository version June 7, 2011; reused E.28 file). Absorption: return response mainly in 08:30-08:35 for gold and silver; copper shows a somewhat delayed response to 08:30 news; for 09:15 releases the peak R-square for gold and silver comes about 30 minutes later; for 10:00 releases a 5-10 minute delay in silver's peak; the response dissipates in less than an hour. Volatility effect decays within about 10 minutes. Authors call the response swift and the metals efficient.
quote: Notably, during the 8:30-8:35 minute interval, the highest adjusted R- square values are found for gold and silver. In contrast, copper exhibits a somewhat delayed response to the 8:30 announcement. For the 9:15 announcements, there is about a 30-minute delay before the realization of the highest adjusted R-square for gold and silver. ... about a 5-10 minute delay in the peak response of silver prices. In all cases, we observe that the metal prices are efficient in incorporating new economic information and the response tends to dissipate in less than an hour after the release of the announcement.
